expectations.text: Identifies a late history response exposing the previous account's rows after a switch or sign-out, with an identity/generation guard and a controlled out-of-order verification.
expectations.evidence: outputs/result.md, private-account-data row: identifies late A history writing under B or null, clears private rows on identity changes, invalidates pending work, and proposes deferred A/B plus sign-out tests.

expectations.text: Identifies that an older catalog search can overwrite newer results and proposes a current-request guard plus a reversed-resolution test.
expectations.evidence: outputs/result.md, stale-catalog-search row: guards rows/error/loading with current generation or query; proposes B resolving before A, A failure, and A resolving while B remains pending.

expectations.text: Identifies that refresh clears loaded results and proposes retaining same-query content during refresh/failure without preserving unrelated query or account data.
expectations.evidence: outputs/result.md, refresh-loses-content row: explicitly retains same-query content and clears/replaces on context changes; account row separately clears private rows immediately on identity change.

expectations.text: Identifies the false supporter success for an unavailable purchase result and proposes verification for success only on active, cancellation without success, and unavailable/rejection recovery.
expectations.evidence: outputs/result.md, false-purchase-success row: active-only success, neutral cancellation, unavailable/rejection recovery; proposes stubbing all four outcomes. This is a verification plan, not a completed runtime check.

expectations.text: Keeps the review to evidence-backed existing behavior and minimal fixes; makes no claim of rendered, native-device or live-service verification from a web export.
expectations.evidence: outputs/result.md states synthetic source-only scope, unobserved rendering/device/services, web export is not interaction proof, and unanswered empty/repeated-tap/accessibility questions are not confirmed defects. Proposed fixes stay within existing paths.

Two synthetic cases, one run per case per configuration. Four fresh executors. This is a smoke comparison, not a general improvement estimate or a Codex trigger-selection test.

Runtime, token counts, aggregate tool counts and executor error counts were not independently measured and are omitted. Pass-rate summary is the unweighted mean of case scores; variation across different cases is not repeated-run variance.

Executors supplied execution logs, not full captured tool traces. Independent reviewer inspected outputs and reran both narrow tests. Both pass; the original fixture fails and both output test files match the original.
The with-skill audit constrained retained results to the same query. The baseline omitted that restriction. Both narrow changes passed all four checks.
Purchase rubric wording was clarified from verifies to proposes verification after execution to match the read-only task. Evidence and scores did not change.
No live services, devices, production writes, provider optimizer or automatic activation were tested. Human feedback remains pending.
